nodes.label: You
nodes.summary: The person whose everyday action starts every trace.

nodes.label: A sandwich
nodes.summary: Two slices of bread (~90 g flour) plus filling. Roughly 450 kcal.

nodes.label: A Claude message
nodes.summary: One prompt and one reply: a few hundred tokens each way.

nodes.label: A hot shower
nodes.summary: About eight minutes under a showerhead, most of it heated water.

nodes.label: Wheat flour
nodes.summary: Milled from wheat grain at ~75% extraction; bran and germ are removed.

nodes.label: Wheat
nodes.summary: Grown on ~220 million hectares worldwide; supplies about a fifth of human calories.

nodes.label: Farmland
nodes.summary: Cropland measured in hectare-years: how much ground, for how long, a harvest occupies.

nodes.label: Nitrogen fertilizer
nodes.summary: Synthetic nitrogen (urea, ammonium nitrate) made from ammonia. Feeds roughly half of humanity.

nodes.label: Crop water
nodes.summary: Rain (green water) and irrigation (blue water) taken up by a growing crop.

nodes.label: Household water
nodes.summary: Treated drinking water delivered to a home; showers are its second-largest indoor use.

nodes.label: Freshwater withdrawals
nodes.summary: All water taken from rivers, lakes and aquifers worldwide, about 4,000 km³ a year.

nodes.label: Datacenter cooling water
nodes.summary: Water evaporated in cooling towers to carry heat away from servers.

nodes.label: Grid electricity
nodes.summary: Power generated and delivered by the grid; its fuel mix sets the carbon cost of every kWh.

nodes.label: Ammonia synthesis
nodes.summary: The Haber-Bosch process: natural gas and air become ammonia at high pressure. Fertilizer's energy bill.

nodes.label: Natural gas
nodes.summary: Methane piped to power plants, factories and homes. Heats about half of US water heaters.

metrics.label: Henry Hub natural gas spot price

nodes.label: Diesel
nodes.summary: The fuel of freight. Nearly every tonne-kilometre of road haulage burns it.

nodes.label: Water heater
nodes.summary: Gas or electric tank in the basement. Water heating is ~18% of a US home's energy use.

nodes.label: Datacenters
nodes.summary: The world's server halls, drawing roughly 1.5% of global electricity and rising fast.

nodes.label: Truck freight
nodes.summary: Road haulage: the last, most energy-intensive leg between mill, bakery and shelf.

nodes.label: Water utility
nodes.summary: Treatment plants and mains that pump drinking water to the tap; a large, invisible electricity user.

nodes.label: Internet backbone
nodes.summary: Long-haul fiber, exchange points and routers that carry packets between networks.

nodes.label: Submarine cables
nodes.summary: About 600 fiber cables on the seabed carrying almost all intercontinental data.

nodes.label: Inference cluster
nodes.summary: Racks of accelerators that run the model when you press send.

nodes.label: GPU accelerator
nodes.summary: The chip that does the matrix math. A single datacenter GPU costs tens of thousands of dollars.

nodes.label: Wheat market
nodes.summary: Global benchmark price for wheat, set by the largest exporters.

nodes.label: Grocery prices
nodes.summary: What US households actually pay for food at home, tracked as an index.

nodes.label: Chip foundry
nodes.summary: The handful of fabs that can make leading-edge logic chips, concentrated in Taiwan.

nodes.label: Utility bill
nodes.summary: Water, gas and electricity charges: the household's price for a shower.

nodes.label: Farm policy
nodes.summary: Crop insurance, price supports and the Farm Bill: why grain costs what it costs.

nodes.label: Chip export controls
nodes.summary: US rules restricting which countries may buy advanced AI chips and the tools to make them.

nodes.label: Showerhead standard
nodes.summary: The federal maximum flow rate for a showerhead, fixed in law since 1992.

edges.why: Two slices of enriched white bread are ~160 kcal; a typical filling brings a whole sandwich to roughly 450 kcal.
A 60 g slice of bread is about 45 g flour by weight after baking, so two slices is ~90 g. Estimate; varies by loaf.
Standard white flour extraction is ~75%: milling removes bran and germ, so 1 kg of flour needs ~1.33 kg of grain.
Global average water footprint of wheat, ~70% of it green water (rainfall) rather than irrigation. Regional values vary widely, hence the range.

edges.unit: t grain per ha per year
edges.why: Global average wheat yield. At 3.6 t/ha, the 120 g of grain in a sandwich occupies about a third of a square metre of field for a year.
Wheat draws down roughly 25 kg of nitrogen per tonne of grain; farms replace most of it with synthetic fertilizer. Rates differ by region and yield.
Nearly all synthetic nitrogen starts as Haber-Bosch ammonia, which uses about 2% of the world's final energy and 1.3% of its CO2. The sandwich's biggest hidden energy cost.

edges.unit: % of ammonia made from natural gas
edges.why: Most ammonia plants reform natural gas for hydrogen; the rest (largely in China) use coal. Gas prices therefore move fertilizer prices, and with a lag, bread prices.
Industrial ovens use roughly 1.1-1.6 MJ per kg of bread baked, i.e. 0.3-0.5 kWh. Two slices is ~0.05 kWh. Estimate from published oven studies; varies by bakery.
A loaded truck burns ~30-35 L per 100 km carrying ~12 t, so each tonne moved one kilometre costs about 30 mL of diesel. Bread's last 20 km cost more energy than the grain's first 1,000 by rail.

edges.unit: % of US freight tonnage moved by truck
edges.why: Trucks carry about three-quarters of US freight by weight, so the retail diesel price is a direct input to the shelf price of anything perishable.

edges.unit: USD of wheat in one sandwich
edges.why: 120 g of grain at the global benchmark price (~US$230 per tonne) is under three cents. Everything else you pay for is milling, baking, labor, energy, rent and margin.

edges.unit: cents of each US food dollar reaching the farm
edges.why: USDA's Food Dollar series: roughly 16 cents of every dollar spent on food goes to farm production. A doubling of wheat prices moves bread prices far less than people expect.

edges.unit: billion USD per year, federal crop insurance
edges.why: The federal crop insurance program cost around US$17 billion in 2022, subsidizing ~60% of premiums. It stabilizes planting decisions, and therefore supply, and therefore the price of your sandwich.
A short question and a paragraph-long answer are a few hundred tokens each way; a token is roughly three-quarters of a word. Estimate; long chats run much higher.

Independent estimates put a typical chatbot query around 0.3 Wh, with Google reporting a 0.24 Wh median for Gemini; large models and long outputs can be ten times that. The most contested number in this graph.

A traceroute from a home connection to a cloud region usually shows 10-20 hops: your ISP, one or two transit networks, then the provider's edge. Estimate; run traceroute yourself to see your own number.
Roughly 600 active submarine cables carry nearly all data between continents; satellites are a rounding error. A message answered in another region touches the seabed.

edges.unit: TWh of global datacenter electricity in 2024
edges.why: About 1.5% of world electricity, projected by the IEA to more than double to ~945 TWh by 2030, with AI the main driver. Your message is a rounding error inside a number that is reshaping grids.

edges.unit: % of US electricity used by datacenters (2023)
edges.why: Up from ~1.9% in 2018; LBNL projects 6.7-12% by 2028. The same grid node the sandwich's bakery draws on, so grid carbon intensity sets the CO2 of both.
Evaporative cooling towers consume about 1.8 L per kWh on site, and power plants upstream withdraw several times more. A 0.3 Wh query is half a millilitre; a fleet is a reservoir.
A single top-end accelerator lists in the tens of thousands of dollars and a cluster holds thousands of them. Capital cost, not electricity, dominates the price of a token.

edges.unit: % of leading-edge logic chips made in Taiwan
edges.why: Below 10 nm, nearly all capacity sits in Taiwan; the GPU answering you was almost certainly fabricated there. Concentration risk expressed as a percentage.

edges.unit: year the first BIS advanced-chip rule took effect
edges.why: Since October 2022 the US has restricted exports of advanced AI chips and chipmaking tools, tightened in 2023 and after. Policy decides who may buy the hardware behind a message.
0.3 Wh at ~US$0.20 per kWh is six thousandths of a cent. Low confidence because it inherits the query-energy estimate; the point is the order of magnitude.
The Water Research Foundation's Residential End Uses study logged flow meters in ~800 homes; the average shower ran 7.8 minutes.
Measured average flow of ~2.1 gallons per minute times 7.8 minutes is about 17 gallons, or 63 litres. Showers are ~20% of indoor household use.

edges.unit: kWh per million gallons treated and delivered
edges.why: Treating and pumping surface water takes around 1,400 kWh per million gallons; groundwater and long pipelines cost more. Your 17 gallons is ~0.02 kWh before it is heated.

edges.unit: % of US electricity used by water and wastewater utilities
edges.why: Moving and cleaning water is one of the largest single electricity uses in most cities, often the biggest line on a municipal power bill.
Raising 63 L of water by ~40°C takes 63 × 4.186 kJ × 40 ≈ 10.5 MJ ≈ 2.9 kWh of heat, before heater losses. Physics, so the range only covers temperature and volume.

edges.unit: % of US homes heating water with natural gas
edges.why: EIA's Residential Energy Consumption Survey: about 47% gas, 46% electric, the rest propane, oil or solar. The Henry Hub price is half of America's shower bill.

edges.unit: % of US homes heating water with electricity
edges.why: For the electric half, a shower is ~3 kWh from the same grid that runs the datacenter and the bakery. Water heating is ~18% of home energy use.
About 10-20 cents of water and sewer, plus ~25 cents of gas or ~60 cents of electricity for heating at current prices. Estimate; utility rates vary by city.

edges.unit: % of global freshwater withdrawals that are municipal
edges.why: Worldwide, households and cities take ~11% of withdrawn freshwater; agriculture takes ~70%. The wheat in your sandwich uses far more water than your shower.
The Energy Policy Act of 1992 capped showerheads at 2.5 gpm; the average measured flow of 2.1 gpm exists because of it. A number in your bathroom set by Congress.
